notes:
dashy 0.8.0

Ten days and 103 commits since 0.7.0. The through-line is that finished work
stops competing with live work, and that dashy says more about its own state
instead of leaving it to be discovered by hand.

Workstreams have a lifecycle. A section of a tracker file can declare itself
active, done, superseded or shaping. Done and superseded work folds behind a
badge in the file view and stops claiming the Next lane, a dated closed section
is marked ready to compact a week later, an end-state record renders where one
exists, and a throughput test names the workstreams that are stuck. The CLI
gained dashy sections, and projects whose tracker files drift from the
convention are reported.

Guesses you can review. What dashy infers about a dashboard now has a review
surface at /p/<id>/guesses, with confirm and reject verbs, a shared tally, and
doors to it from the Should lane, the Overview chip, the sidebar and settings.

Connectors you can configure in the app. Secrets have a real form and
secret_ref resolves to a value, a declared cadence becomes a real timer, silence
escalates, and the Jira collector gained its fetch half.

Diagnostics that measure instead of guess. A storage panel shows file sizes and
row counts, a Rendering row says whether the browser is drawing through the
GPU (the usual reason Grid Mode drops frames), and the config repo reports its
identity, git state and any stray clones.

Also in this release: the Override control was rebuilt with words and
backend-scoped models in the row, live Claude Code sessions rank in the
attention model, the attention model is served as JSON for a desktop widget,
and Grid Mode stops paying for an empty overlay and a repainting floor.

A sweep of 84 open review items closed with validation and trust-boundary
fixes, template and accessibility fixes, AA contrast for archived and tertiary
text in every theme, and a named codec at every text subprocess call.

Upgrading needs no manual step and there are no new schema migrations. Two
things behave differently: a DASHY_DATA_DIR that points inside the workspace
without a leading dot, or at a foreign git repo, now stops startup with an error
instead of being used, and folded nested lists in the file view open unfolded
once, because the fold store changed its key.

Known and shipping unfixed, for the fourth release running: the Windows build
bundles keyring without its backends, so provider credentials fall back to
dashy's own file store rather than Credential Manager. Nothing is lost and the
fallback is the designed one.
